title: Quiz: floating point
prompt: The callee-saved `d` registers, the `fmov` immediate range, conversions between integers and floats, and the fused multiply-add family.

questions.question: When a subroutine saves the callee-saved floating-point registers d8 to d15 on the stack, how much of the underlying 128-bit hardware register must actually be preserved?
questions.explanation: The calling convention makes a callee preserve v8 through v15, but only the low 64 bits of each one. Those low 64 bits are exactly the d8 to d15 view, so storing the d register saves everything a caller is allowed to depend on.
questions.hint: You only need to save the part that holds a double.

questions.question: What restriction applies to the immediate value in an fmov that loads a floating-point constant into a register?
options: It must be +/- n/16 * 2^r, with n from 16 to 31 and r from -3 to +4.
It must be a whole number, because the fraction bits are not encoded in the instruction.
It must be positive, because the sign has to be added afterwards with a separate fneg.
It must be an exact power of two, since only the exponent fits into the 8-bit field.
questions.explanation: The fmov immediate is packed into 8 bits, so only a small set of constants encodes exactly: +/- n/16 * 2^r with n in 16 to 31 and r in -3 to +4. Anything outside that set is loaded from memory instead, usually a .double in .data reached with an ldr.
questions.hint: The encoding is 8 bits total: 1 sign bit, 3 exponent bits, 4 fraction bits.

questions.question: Which instruction converts a single-precision float into the nearest 32-bit signed integer?
questions.explanation: fcvtns Wd, Sn reads the single in Sn and writes the nearest signed integer to Wd, with ties going to even. fcvtnu produces an unsigned result, scvtf runs the other direction from integer to float, and fcvt only changes precision between float formats.
questions.hint: Read the mnemonic as float convert, nearest, signed.

questions.question: The instruction fmsub d4, d5, d6, d7 executes. Which formula does it apply?
questions.explanation: fmsub subtracts the product of the first two source registers from the fourth operand, so d4 = d7 - (d5 * d6). It is a fused operation, meaning the product is not rounded before the subtraction, and fmadd is the same shape with the product added instead.
questions.hint: The last operand is the value being subtracted from, not the value being subtracted.

questions.question: Which instruction converts a 64-bit signed integer into a double-precision float?
questions.explanation: scvtf Dd, Xn reads Xn as a two's complement signed value and writes the equivalent double to Dd. ucvtf would read the same bits as unsigned, and fmov Dd, Xn copies the 64 bits unchanged so they are reinterpreted as a double's bit pattern rather than converted.
questions.hint: Read the mnemonic as signed convert to float.
